1. Implementation

The document has been created and approved by the General Assembly of 29.11.2025.
The document and its rules will be implemented from the 2029 season (01/01/2029).
Competitors will have 3 seasons to align their equipment with this document and its rules.

2. Definition

Sallets are the evolution of bascinets as the main combat helmet.

Earliest examples are dated from 1430, and sallets were in use until 1540. The designs have widely
evolved throughout the years.

Sallets are widely used in western Europe and can be made with integral face protection or open-faced
helmets.

Sallets are worn alone or with an addition of a bevor, of plate or mail.
Bevor is a plate or chainmail element of armor designed to protect the neck and the mouth.
Sallets are Denied for 14th century and Transitional armors.

Due to the extraordinary range of variety in 15th century armors, it is not possible to give a single
approved status.

Sallets are Approved if matching the rest of armor for mid-15th century, Transitional 15-16th and
first part of 16th century armor.

Chainmail bevor Plate bevor

pages.text:
4. Requirements

4.1. General Requirements

Reproductions must closely resemble the appearance and proportions of historical sources.
A particular attention must be paid to the crest on top of the sallet, often forgotten by modern armorers.

y

Any metal part of the helmet must conform to the “Armors and Weapons Aesthetics and Decorations
document.

Any textile or leather part of the helmet must conform to the “Textiles and Leather” document.

4.2. Visor

Visors must not be too long or too short, it must respect the proportions of historical sources.

Visors locking systems must be reproduced as per historical sources. It must be hidden in helmet
construction if it is not based on historical sources.

It is Allowed to weld the visor down. Welded visors must resemble a functional removable visor.
Breath holes should be round, square or rectangular.

Round breath holes must not exceed a diameter of 10 mm.

Square or rectangular breath holes must replicate historical sources.

Breath holes must not be so numerous that they compromise the helm’s structural integrity. It is
acceptable to mirror breath holes to both sides.

Breath holes of another shape must be documented by historical sources to be Allowed.

4.3. Eyes and Mouth slot

Eye slots must resemble sources for the visor.

Eye slots should not exceed 25mm tall to prevent any injury.
It is Allowed to add up to five (5) safety eyebars.

Eye bars must be welded internally or riveted internally.

Eye bars must conform to the “Eye bars” document.

4.4. Bevor

Sallets are not designed to be worn with an aventail, unlike bascinets. Sallets are worn with bevor.

Sallet must be worn with a plate bevor, or a safe construction simulating a mail bevor as best as
possible.

Bevor must be constructed in such a way as to protect its wearer. Mail bevor must integrate a grill of
protection or additional plates.

Chainmail bevor must conform to Chainmail Aventails requirements listed in the “Aventails” document.
Additional neck protection can be worn according to historical sources.
Additional neck protection not based on historical sources can be worn if concealed.

pages.text:
4.5. Others

Sallets may be decorated in the spirit of medieval styles, such as orle, torse, vervelle covers and coat of
arms badges etc.

Such decoration must be made in coherence with historical sources.

Sallets can be covered with silk or velvet, as per historical sources. These decorations require a lot of
maintenance to maintain a high level of aesthetic. Any Sallet with silk or velvet cover that is too much
damaged can be denied during Authenticity Check.

Using modern and/or offensive imagery and slogans is prohibited.
